body:
After a good night out for a friend's birthday, my girlfriend and I went home very very drunk. When we rolled into the house I remembered about a gram of bk-2-CB I had hidden away, so being the idiot I am I decided that me and my girl should have some right now. Stupid idea.
I took the powder out and filled a cigarette paper with as much as I could fit in it and swallowed it down, I gave my girlfriend much less but at the time I had no idea what I was doing. Then we both went to bed.
A few hours later I woke up with a stinking hangover but felt a little strange.... Then I remembered what I had done. Oh shit! I ran downstairs and looked at the packet. There was only a couple of hundred milligrams left. I must have taken at least half a gram. I looked at the time and realised it had only been 4 hours ago and it was only just starting.
An hour or so later I started to feel hot like I had a fever. I had strong CEVs with psychedelic patterns and faces. I didn't feel good, I felt ill. For the next hour things were getting stronger and stronger until about 6 to 7 hours post dosing. I had strong OEV, everything was morphing and changing. I could see patterns and colours so much that I could barely see, my heart was pounding in my chest. I looked down at my arms and they looked swollen and deformed. Then I totally lost my grip on reality.
I was lost in a psychedelic universe, I didn't know if my eyes were open or closed. I had no sense of self other than the fact I knew I was very ill. Time passed slowly and this feeling felt like it lasted an eternity. Slowly I felt myself returning to reality but I knew I was still pretty messed up, it felt more like delirium rather than anything enjoyable. I somehow managed to take my temperature, 39.6C. I couldn't read the clock and had no real grip on time. This went on for what a later worked out was around 16 hours of pure hell.
I learnt one thing from this whole experience. Never ever do something this stupid. My best guess is that I took somewhere between 500 and 700mg. I am thankful I survived.
